Slice I completed: NLE Keyboard Transport (ArrowLeft/Right +/-1s, Shift +/-5s, ArrowUp/Down clip stepping, Home/End bounds), J/K/L shuttle controls (J=-2s, K=pause, L=play/toggle), global 1/2/3 stage navigation with strict input focus guard, Storyboard-to-Timeline 1-click focus hand-off, and .tl-shortcuts-hint HUD tooltip in style.css/index.html (inline style count kept at 15/19). 8 contract tests added in tests/test_timeline_keyboard.py, all 8 verified with Rule 4 deliberate break mutations. Full suite: 1273 passed, 1 xfailed (0 regressions).

Slice I reviewed and committed: keyboard transport, J/K/L shuttle, 1/2/3 stage navigation, storyboard focus hand-off, shortcuts HUD. Antigravity's 8 tests are genuine - 11 of 12 independent mutations were caught. Review found a real crash the 8 tests missed: End computed the film total itself, bypassing timelineSeek's empty-film guard, so End on the 'no film loaded' Timeline threw a TypeError. The same unguarded read sat on the play path, so Space crashed there too. Both closed with the file's own tlPictures() idiom; 2 regression tests added and mutation-verified. 10 keyboard tests, full suite 1274 passed, 1 xfailed.

Slice J complete: Anchored zoom on playhead, centering when playhead is outside viewport, fitTimelineToWindow with (clientWidth - 24) / total calculation and [1, 60] clamping, safe empty-film guard, keyboard multiplicative zoom (+/= 1.5x, -/_ /1.5) and keyboard 0 fit gated under active timeline pane. Closed Slice H caption auto-scroll gap in tests/test_timeline_zoom.py. Measured Job 4 Before Adam 347-line benchmark: 1.09ms (zoom 8) and 2.33ms (zoom 60), 59 slider drag events. All 8 Rule 4 deliberate break mutations caught. Full test suite: 1283 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failures.

Slice J reviewed and committed with no code fixes needed - a first for this run. Ten independent mutations were run against the eight new tests and all ten were caught, including hoisting 0 above the timeline gate and disabling the caption auto-scroll. Slice I's null-script crash shape was correctly guarded on every new key. Two process gaps recorded rather than buried: the live verification gate was skipped and not reported as skipped, and Job 4's benchmark left no script and no artifact. One measured limitation, caused by Slice J's brief rather than its code: the [1,60] zoom clamp means Fit cannot fit an 18-minute film (total=1080s, zoom=1, lane=1080px, viewport=800px). Slice K addresses all three. Suite 1283 passed, 1 xfailed.

Committed CLAUDE.md and Slice K Job 1 live verification gate. The gate clears the debt Slices I and J carried: every Slice I key passes in the real browser and Slice J anchoring drifts 0.22px. It also confirmed live that Fit does not fit (zoom 1, lanes 1160 vs client 823). Slice K Job 2 WITHDRAWN: the artifact measured scrollLeft_after 68167 against max 68758, so no clamping occurred and the 0.27px drift is sub-pixel rounding, not truncation - the artifact note claiming otherwise contradicts its own numbers. The premise was wrong in principle too, since a clamp to max leaves the playhead at playhead_px - laneWidth + clientWidth, always on screen. Slice K revised down to the zoom floor fix. Antigravity stopped after Job 1 without code changes and without handing the token back; the revised brief spells out the handback steps.

Slice K closed by Claude at the owner's instruction. Job 1 (live verification gate) was Antigravity's and cleared the debt Slices I and J carried. Job 2 was WITHDRAWN - the artifact measured scrollLeft_after 68167 against max 68758, so no clamping occurred and the 0.27px drift was sub-pixel rounding; the premise was wrong in principle too, since a clamp to max leaves the playhead at playhead_px - laneWidth + clientWidth, always on screen. Job 3 shipped: zoom floor 1 -> 0.2 px/s in setTimelineZoom and #tl-zoom's min, plus step=any which solved Job 4 outright by making slider and tlZoom agree exactly. The existing clamp test asserted the old floor and was split rather than relaxed: a 33-minute film must now survive unclamped at 0.4, and a 5000s film must still clamp at 0.2. Three tests added, five mutations run, five caught. Suite 1286 passed, 1 xfailed - 1283 + 3 exactly, no regressions from widening the zoom range.

Slice L complete: Job 1 live DOM measured on Before Adam (zoom 0.689, 7 overflowing clip heads, narrowest clip 10px; recorded in reports/verification_gate/slice_l_dom.json). Job 2 boundary handles escaped parent clip to straddle clip seams in laneP with min 8px hit area, overlap suppression (later boundary wins), and keyboard/ARIA accessibility fully preserved. Job 3 micro-clip label threshold (< 24px) omits text while keeping hover titles. Job 4 zoomTimelineToSelection mapped to '.' key under timeline pane gate with [0.2, 60] clamp and safe no-op on empty selection/film. 8 contract tests added in tests/test_timeline_low_zoom.py, all 7 Rule 4 deliberate break mutations caught and restored cleanly. Full test suite: 1293 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failures.

Slice L reviewed and committed. Handles now render into the lane at the seam with translateX(-50%) instead of nested inside an overflow:hidden clip, with 8px overlap suppression, a micro-label threshold at 24px, and zoomTimelineToSelection on the dot key. Nine of ten independent mutations caught; the one escape was correct, since the tlSelected guard is redundant against the pic check below it. Review found one regression the slice introduced: timelineHandlePointerMove updates currClip.style.left but never handle.style.left, which was free when the handle was a child of the clip and is not now, so the handle sat still while the edge slid away. No test drove pointermove. Fixed with the file's own idiom, since tlSfxDragState already moves its handle that way, plus two tests: one drives a real drag, one asserts handles are emitted after every clip because the CSS assertion alone cannot catch a nested cropped handle. The slice_l_dom.json artifact independently confirms Slice K in a real browser: actually_fits true, 799 against 823. Suite 1296 passed, 1 xfailed.

milestone_note: Milestone 3 is ACTIVE and Slice M is its LAST slice. I gave the Timeline a keyboard, J anchored the zoom, K lowered the floor and cleared the live-verification debt, L made the handles survive that floor. Every one of those makes an edit easier to perform and none of them makes one reversible - there is no undo anywhere in the app. Slice M adds it, then the relay stops at the owner gate before Milestone 4.

driver.cannot_spawn: Antigravity has no CLI entry point here. The driver notifies and waits when the token is with the builder. Set builder_command in config/relay_loop.json if that ever changes.
driver.milestone_gate: Stops at phase=MILESTONE_COMPLETE or ready_for=OWNER and waits for a phone ack.

review_findings: Slice L introduced, and review caught, a drag regression invisible to every test: moving the handle out of the clip meant it stopped riding along when the clip's left edge moved, and nothing drove pointermove. The lesson is that a structural move needs a test for the behaviour the old structure was providing for free.

Slice L Job 1 recorded narrow_handle: null - the measurement the brief called the number the slice turns on - and Job 2 proceeded unchanged rather than reshaping as the brief instructed. The artifact was also taken only at fit zoom (0.689 px/s), where narrowest_clip.offsetWidth is 10px, the same as the handle width, so nothing was cropped at the zoom measured. Job 2 was right in principle but is not evidenced by the artifact.
Test quality is holding: Slice J 10/10 on independent mutation, K 5/5, L 9/10 with a correct escape. The Slice G and H pattern of tests that could not fail has not recurred in four slices.
known_gaps: There is no undo anywhere in the app. A case-insensitive grep for undo or redo across frontend/app.js returns 0 hits. Slice M.
The global keydown listener checks no modifiers, so Ctrl+1 switches panes and Ctrl+0 fits. Slice M Job 3 fixes it, since that slice opens the listener anyway.

moveTimelinePictureBoundary mutates coverageReport.shot_reports alongside the script and does not go through persistCurrentScript at all. Any snapshot scheme hooked into the persistence layer would therefore miss boundary moves, the most visible edit, and would leave the coverage report drifting from the script. Slice M Jobs 2 and 4.

The three picture-boundary deltas from Slice H Job 3, and Slice J Job 4's render benchmark, were both reported as numbers with no script and no artifact. Same shape twice. If either matters, measure again and record it.
